_comment: WHERE EVERY DECLARED-SECRET NAME'S VALUE ACTUALLY COMES FROM. Read and checked
by .ci/scripts/quality/check_secret_supply.py; read that module's docstring before
editing, because every rule below is enforced there and none of it is advisory.
NO VALUE OF ANY KIND IS RECORDED HERE. Names, kinds, destinations and one project
UUID that .ci/config/bws-secret-map.json already carries in the clear. .ci/lib/
bws-env.sh:16-18 states the same rule for the fetch helper and is the reason it
holds for this file too: this repository is public and a gate's output is a log
surface.
TWO HALVES, AND THEY ARE DELIBERATELY IN ONE FILE.
`residue` is DERIVED and then classified: the names env-manifest.json puts in the
`secret` shard that .ci/config/bws-secret-map.json does not hold. `secret` means
'supplied by the vault or by a GitHub secret', so a name in that shard which no
vault holds is a name whose supply is UNSTATED. Every one gets a kind and a
reason here. The gate asserts set equality with the derived residue in BOTH
directions, so this half can neither be trimmed to escape a finding nor
pre-loaded with one.
`dotenv` is the TRUNCATION SPEC for private/account/.env -- one destination per
assigned name, set-equal with the file while it exists. The terminal state is NO
FILE AT ALL (agent/plans/PLAN-account-env-to-bws.md T18): the bootstrap token
lives in ${XDG_CONFIG_HOME:-~/.config}/rediacc/bws-access-token, and every
other destination is a place the value comes from instead.
`consumers` is the THIRD half: the named profiles `python3 -m
rediacc_ci.core.bws_env exec --profile P -- CMD` binds into a child process
(account-dev, account-e2e, deploy-bench, rotation, backup-plane, publish-media).
Each spec uses the `NAME > LOCAL` grammar; the gate asserts every NAME resolves
in the vault map and that no spec is a wildcard.
THE HALVES CHECK EACH OTHER, WHICH IS WHY THEY SHARE A FILE. A `ci-shared`
destination is FALSE unless the vault map holds the name, a `ci-shared-alias`
destination is FALSE unless the map holds the name its `aliases` row names, and a
`dev.defaults.env` destination is FALSE if the map holds the name. A name headed for
the COMMITTED defaults file that is classified `secret` is a credential about to be
committed, and the gate refuses it by name.
ONE PROJECT, AND THE OPERATOR RULED IT STAYS ONE (2026-09-24, PLAN-account-env-to-bws
Q1, Q2, Q4). The dev keypair is seeded as `_DEV` names, the admin credentials sit
beside everything else, and the dev SES key is an alias of the EU entry. No
`dev-shared` or `admin-bootstrap` project exists or is planned.
AND THE GATE STARTS ENFORCING THE SEEDED STATE THE MOMENT THE PROJECT EXISTS. A
seeded name lands in bws-secret-map.json on the next refresh, leaves the derived
residue, and its entry here reds as RESOLVED with instructions to drain it. No
edit to the gate is needed for that to happen.
HOW TO ADD OR REMOVE AN ENTRY. Do neither by hand-writing a set. The gate names
the exact name and the exact half, and there is deliberately no bulk reseed verb:
a blanket rewrite is how a fresh violation gets absorbed alongside a legitimate
drain, and 75 entries is small enough to edit one line at a time.

kinds.runner-minted: Minted per job by GitHub Actions or by an action, and never stored anywhere. A vault entry for one of these would be a second, longer-lived credential for something the runner already hands out with a one-hour life.
kinds.sdk-alias: Not a credential of its own: the spelling an SDK insists on, exported at the call site from a name a vault DOES hold. `alias_of` names that entry and the gate checks it resolves in .ci/config/bws-secret-map.json, so an alias cannot point at nothing.
kinds.generated: Produced at run time by the process that consumes it: a key pair written into a temp dir, a token seeded into a preview database, a password composed for a throwaway container. There is no value to store, only a recipe.
kinds.user-supplied: Typed by the END USER of the shipped product on their own machine. It is in the secret shard because it carries a secret value; it is not in any vault because it is not our value.
kinds.fixture-default: Has a non-secret default committed in the tree, so an unset environment still runs. Storing it would give a fixture a credential.
kinds.github-secret-only: Lives as a GitHub Actions secret and was deliberately not mirrored into the vault. The BLOCKER for each is in `why`.
kinds.not-a-credential: In the secret shard but not a secret: a name fragment, a suffix, a switch. Recorded here rather than quietly reshuffled between shards, because moving it is `check:ci-env-manifest`'s call and not this gate's.
kinds.bootstrap-irreducible: The credential that fetches the others. It cannot come from the store it unlocks. Exactly one name may carry this kind and the gate enforces that.
kinds.dev-shared: A real development credential with no dev store to come from. The project `dev-shared` does not exist -- the live vault holds ONE project, `ci-shared` -- and only the web vault can create it, so this is door:operator-only. Every entry with this kind is PRINTED BY NAME on every run.

AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID.why: the AWS SDK reads only this spelling; the deploy scripts export it from the R2 key immediately before calling the SDK.

AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY.why: the secret half of the pair above, exported at the same two lines.

AWS_SES_ACCESS_KEY_ID.why: The Worker binding name, fed from the regional vault entry AWS_SES_ACCESS_KEY_ID_EU in CI. On a developer machine `bws_env exec --profile account-dev` binds the same entry under this name (`AWS_SES_ACCESS_KEY_ID_EU > AWS_SES_ACCESS_KEY_ID`), on the operator's ruling to keep aliasing the EU key rather than mint a dev IAM user (agent/plans/PLAN-account-env-to-bws.md Q4).

AWS_SES_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY.why: The Worker binding name, fed from the regional vault entry AWS_SES_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY_EU in CI. On a developer machine `bws_env exec --profile account-dev` binds the same entry under this name (`AWS_SES_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY_EU > AWS_SES_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY`), on the operator's ruling to keep aliasing the EU key rather than mint a dev IAM user (agent/plans/PLAN-account-env-to-bws.md Q4).

BWS_ACCESS_TOKEN.why: the fetcher refuses without it and says why in as many words: no bws verb mints or rotates a machine-account token, so the credential that opens the store cannot be kept in the store. It lives in its own token file (`bws_env.token_path()`, ${XDG_CONFIG_HOME:-~/.config}/rediacc/bws-access-token, mode 0600), never in private/account/.env (agent/plans/PLAN-account-env-to-bws.md T1).

CHECKS_TOKEN.why: detect-pointer-bump.sh documents it as `plain GITHUB_TOKEN; checks:read on console` and ci.yml supplies github.token. The runner mints it.

DOCKERHUB_PASSWORD.why: BLOCKER: an anonymous Docker Hub pull works and the gate says so at its own :29 -- the credential only raises the rate limit. Mirroring it into the vault would put a third-party account password in a store every CI job can read, to buy a quota.

E2E_ACCOUNT_API_TOKEN.why: start-account-for-e2e.sh CREATES the subscribed user and echoes the resulting bearer token into GITHUB_ENV. It exists for one suite run against one throwaway account server.

E2E_SSH_KEY.why: a path to a key file, defaulted with `??` in every reading test. The key is the one the e2e machine was provisioned with, not a stored secret.

GH_APP_TOKEN.why: the app-token action's output again, under a second spelling, used to rewrite a git URL for the submodule fetch.

GH_TOKEN.why: the gh CLI's own variable. Every site sets it inline from a token minted moments earlier; nothing reads a stored value.

GITHUB_PAT.why: documented at that file's :30 as `app token; contents:read on the submodule repos`. The name says PAT and the value is an App token, which is worth knowing and is not worth a vault entry.

GITHUB_TOKEN.why: the runner's own per-job token. It is in the secret shard because it carries a credential; it can never be in a vault.

MATRIX_SECRET_SUFFIX.why: a region suffix, `EU` or `US` or `ASIA`, used to BUILD the name of a secret. resolve-account-deploy-config.sh requires it with `:?` and assigns it straight to SUFFIX. It is arguably misfiled in the secret shard; that is check:ci-env-manifest's call, so it is recorded here instead of moved.

PGPASSWORD.why: the Rediaccfile composes it for a tutorial's throwaway Postgres container and hands the same value to the app. Nothing outside that one deployment ever sees it.

REDIACC_CONFIG_PASSWORD.why: documented to users as the password-slot secret for headless remote-config unlock. It is the user's password for the user's config, and this repository must never hold one.

REDIACC_MASTER_PASSWORD.why: read at config-file-storage.ts before falling back to the interactive resolver. Same argument: it is the user's value.

REDIACC_TOKEN.why: the account api-token for whoever is running the CLI. CI paths get theirs from E2E_ACCOUNT_API_TOKEN or SMOKE_TEST_TOKEN, both generated.

RUSTFS_ACCESS_KEY.why: the compose file defaults it to `rustfsadmin` in four places. It is the login of a local S3 stand-in that listens on a loopback port.

RUSTFS_SECRET_KEY.why: the secret half of the pair above, with the same committed default.

SMOKE_TEST_TOKEN.why: seed-smoke-test.sh SEEDS the token into the preview D1 and echoes it to GITHUB_OUTPUT. It is created and consumed inside one run.

SSH_KEY.why: a PATH to a key file under $RUNNER_TEMP, which check:ci-workflows quotes as its own plant fixture. The key is generated by the staging provision step.

TOKEN.why: check_bws_map.py's GH_CLI_ENV names it beside APP_TOKEN and REPO as a gh-CLI passthrough. A bare `TOKEN` is never a stored name.

TUTORIAL_SSH_KEY.why: defaulted at tutorial-helpers.sh to $HOME/.renet/staging/.ssh/id_rsa. A path to a key the VM lab made, not a value.

NFPM_APK_KEY_FILE.why: build_linux_pkg.py sets this itself at run time from the GPG material already unsealed for the release (see the os.environ[...] assignments around line 539). It is never stored: the value exists only inside the signing process that consumes it, so a vault entry would be a second, longer-lived copy of a credential that currently lives for the length of one build.

NFPM_DEB_KEY_FILE.why: build_linux_pkg.py sets this itself at run time from the GPG material already unsealed for the release (see the os.environ[...] assignments around line 539). It is never stored: the value exists only inside the signing process that consumes it, so a vault entry would be a second, longer-lived copy of a credential that currently lives for the length of one build.

NFPM_DEB_PASSPHRASE.why: build_linux_pkg.py sets this itself at run time from the GPG material already unsealed for the release (see the os.environ[...] assignments around line 539). It is never stored: the value exists only inside the signing process that consumes it, so a vault entry would be a second, longer-lived copy of a credential that currently lives for the length of one build.

NFPM_RPM_KEY_FILE.why: build_linux_pkg.py sets this itself at run time from the GPG material already unsealed for the release (see the os.environ[...] assignments around line 539). It is never stored: the value exists only inside the signing process that consumes it, so a vault entry would be a second, longer-lived copy of a credential that currently lives for the length of one build.

NFPM_RPM_PASSPHRASE.why: build_linux_pkg.py sets this itself at run time from the GPG material already unsealed for the release (see the os.environ[...] assignments around line 539). It is never stored: the value exists only inside the signing process that consumes it, so a vault entry would be a second, longer-lived copy of a credential that currently lives for the length of one build.

APK_RSA_PRIVATE_KEY.why: BLOCKER: NOTHING SUPPLIES THIS TODAY, and the kind is the closest of the nine rather than a claim that a GitHub secret currently holds it -- read this `why`, not the kind. apk is declared-unsigned: check-release-signing-coverage.sh carries the exemption and records it as VERIFIED 2026-09-06 by building both ways, and build_linux_pkg.py says in its own words that APK_RSA_PRIVATE_KEY is set by nothing here and is absent from bws-secret-map.json, so nfpm.yaml's apk signature block reads an env var never populated. It stays in the `secret` shard because the name carries key material the day anyone mints one. Mint an RSA key, put it in the vault, and both this entry and that exemption go.

destinations.token-file: The bootstrap token's own file, ${XDG_CONFIG_HOME:-~/.config}/rediacc/bws-access-token (mode 0600), which `bws_env.read_token()` reads when the variable is unset. Only a `bootstrap_names` credential may route here.
destinations.ci-shared: Already in the vault under the same name. The local assignment is a DUPLICATE, deleted once `compare` reports MATCH and its readers bind it through a `consumers` profile. The gate checks the name really is in .ci/config/bws-secret-map.json.
destinations.ci-shared-alias: In the vault under ANOTHER name, which `aliases` records (`STORE > LOCAL` in a profile). The gate checks every such row has an alias and that the alias target is in .ci/config/bws-secret-map.json.
destinations.dev.defaults.env: Not a secret. Moves to the COMMITTED private/account/dev.defaults.env, which then IS the documentation. The gate refuses any name here that the env manifest classifies `secret`, because that is a credential one commit away from being public.
destinations.derived: Computed at run time from GATEWAY_PORT by the process that needs it (account_dev passes WEBAUTHN_ORIGIN to the gateway; rdc.sh --dev reads the port from .account-state). Nothing stores it.
destinations.dead: Empty in the file, and every reader treats empty as unset (private/account/src/entry/on-premise.ts), so deleting the line changes nothing.

account-dev.why: `./run.sh account dev` (.ci/lib/account.sh account_dev) re-execs itself under this profile. The six DEV signing and session keys are required; everything else only switches on an optional feature, so a store without it still starts the gateway. CI's drills leg mints throwaway keys into the job environment instead, and the shell wins.

account-e2e.why: `./run.sh account test e2e` (account_test_e2e). The suite drives a running gateway; the one value it takes from the store is the root address the admin tests log in as.

backup-plane.why: programs/backup-storage/start-local-plane.sh starts a dev gateway against a local RustFS. It needs the DEV keys and nothing else: ACCOUNT_BACKUP_S3_* are exported by the script itself, which is why this profile must never grow a wildcard.

deploy-bench.why: scripts/ops/deploy-bench.sh pushes the bench Worker's secrets. Bench signs with the DEV keypair (what private/account/.env held), uses its own SES and Turnstile credentials, and runs `rotation check --for=bench`, which needs the admin set.

rotation.why: `./run.sh rotation ...` (account_rotation). The admin credentials mint and delete infrastructure; the operator ruled they live in ci-shared (Q2). `passes_token` hands the bootstrap token to the child because the rotation tool writes `bitwarden-sm:` consumers with `bws` itself. `CLOUDFLARE_TURNSTILE_SECRET_KEY` is optional: `rotation check` probes it through siteverify for the `turnstile` slug (scripts/rotation/commands/check.ts) and falls back to a timestamp heuristic that reports a false drift without it.

publish-media.why: The R2 media sync and `--publish-www` upload to media.rediacc.com. Without these the run copies locally, uploads nothing and exits 0, which is why .claude/rediacc_hooks/guards/block_host_toolchain_run.py demands the profile in the command.

credential-drift.why: `npm run check:env-credential-drift`, the advisory phase of ./run.sh setup. It compares the IDENTIFIERS local development uses against private/account/rotation-manifest.json. All optional, so a machine with no bootstrap token skips loudly instead of failing setup.

r2-artifacts.why: scripts/ops/r2-oneshot-scrub.sh and other local R2 artifact-bucket maintenance run by hand. The same three names CI requests for artifact uploads.

publish-solutions.why: private/growth/video_pipeline/publish-solutions.sh: uploads the solution videos to R2 (the media keys) and purges the CDN (the Cloudflare global key). It used to `source` the whole account env file for five names.
